page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.32-512 is a flexible compute instance configured for memory-intensive enterprise operations. The platform is driven by an Intel Xeon 8358 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Sized with 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs via hardware hyperthreading, the compute core allocation includes L1 data cache of 32 KB, L2 cache of 4 MB, and L3 cache of 16 MB. The instance features hardware support for AVX-512, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2 instruction sets, but does not bundle any GPU accelerators.

Memory capacity is a defining characteristic of this configuration, supplying 512 GB of system RAM that equates to an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Storage architecture relies entirely on external volumes, as the instance includes no local NVMe or bundled disk storage. The server is allocated one complimentary public IPv4 address. Networked storage attachments must be accounted for during deployment to handle all persistent disk input and output requirements.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong throughput in specialized data handling tasks. The system achieves a top-tier multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 283.34 GB/sec and static web serving throughput of 57.71 GB/sec. Small-model LLM prompt processing reaches 2467.58 tokens per second. Standard compute metrics register within median ranges, including stress-ng multi-core scores of 58242.52 and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 166.98 GB/sec. Redis operations process within the median tier at 51.57 million operations per second.

The instance delivers high resource density for environments that require vast memory pools without provisioning dedicated bare-metal hardware. Because CPU and memory are scaled flexibly, this 1:8 core-to-memory configuration provides qualitative efficiency for memory-bound applications. The primary tradeoff centers on the absence of bundled local storage, requiring network block volumes for file operations. The platform is best matched with in-memory caching systems, distributed data analysis, enterprise web tier workloads, and large Redis instances.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.32-512 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 64 dedicated virtual cores derived from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8358 processor running at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the platform includes AVX-512 extensions, SHA-NI cryptography, and dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 512 GB of system memory, providing 8 GB per vCPU. The server has no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, requiring remote block volumes for persistent data. Benchmark assessments reveal strong performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 283.34 GB/sec and static web serving throughput reaching 57.71 GB/sec, while multi-core stress-ng tests place within median industry tiers. VM.Standard3.Flex.32-512 is structured for memory-intensive workloads, including large in-memory databases, Redis deployments, batch decompression pipelines, and high-concurrency web services.
